senses.gloss: b. h.;v. Ges. H. Dict. s. v.) [to join sign to sign,] to compose, write; to promise in writing, to will, assign, consign.
units: <cite ref="Gittin 20a:11">Gitt. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>וכ׳ ולא חקק</he> it says (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 24:1">Deut. XXIV, 1</cite>) ‘and he shall write’ but not engrave; Y. ib. II, 44ᵇ top, v. <cite ref="K01358"><he>כְּתִיבָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Makkot 3:6">Macc. III, 6</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 19:28">Lev. XIX, 28</cite>) <he>עד שׁיִכְתּוֹב וכ׳</he> unless he writes (designs) and etches with ink, stibium or anything that marks; Sifra K’doshim, Par. 3, ch. VI, v. <cite ref="K01351"><he>כְּתוֹבֶת</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Megillah 9a:11">Meg. 9ᵃ</cite> <he>כִּתְבוּ לי תורת וכ׳</he> write (translate) for me the Law &c.
<cite ref="Megillah 7a:5">Ib. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>כִּתְבוּנִי בספר</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>לדורות</he>) write me down (record my deeds) in a book (Book of Esther).
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 47:3">Ex. R. s. 47</cite>, beg. <he>כְּתוֹב אתה</he> write thou thyself.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 12:3">Sabb. XII, 3</cite> <he>הכּוֹתֵב וכ׳</he> he who writes two letters (on the Sabbath). Ib. 5 <he>נתכוין לִכְתּוֹב ח״ית</he> if he intended to write a Ḥeth.—

<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 9:1">Keth. IX, 1</cite> <he>הכּוֹתֵב לאשתו וכ׳</he> he who declares to his wife &c.; <cite ref="Ketubot 83a:4">ib. 83ᵃ</cite> <he>תני ר׳ חייא האומר</he> R. Ḥ. interpreted it, ‘he who says’ (verbally).
<cite ref="Ketubot 102b:6">Ib. 102ᵇ</cite> <he>מאי כּוֹתְבִין אומרים</he> ‘they write’ (in the Mishnah) means merely they declare.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 5:1">Ib. V, 1</cite> <he>והיא כוֹתֶבֶת וכ׳</he> and she may write (a receipt), I have received &c.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 50b:10">Pes. 50ᵇ</cite> <he>כּוֹתְבֵי ספרים וכ׳</he> copyists of sacred books, or T’fillin &c.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 14b:12">B. Bath. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>משה כ׳ ספרו וכ׳</he> Moses is the author of his book, the chapter of Balaam, and the Book of Job; a. v. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="K01347"><he>כָּתוּב</he></cite>, f. <cite ref="K01350"><he>כְּתוּבָה</he></cite>; pl. <he>כְּתוּבִים</he>, <he>כְּתוּבִין</he>; <he>כְּתוּבוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Megillah 31a:12">Meg. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>דבר זה כ׳ בתורה וכ׳</he> this is written in the Law, and repeated in the Prophets &c.
<cite ref="Megillah 7a:3">Ib. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>כבר כ׳ אני וכ׳</he> I am already recorded in the chronicles of &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 6:1:14">Y. Shek. VI, 49ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>כיצד היו הלוחות כ׳</he> how was the writing on the tablets arranged?—

<cite ref="Gittin 54b:15">Gitt. 54ᵇ</cite> <he>כל ס״ת … כ׳ לשמן</he> any scroll of the Law in which the Divine names are not written with full consciousness, v. <cite ref="U01408"><he>שֵׁם</he></cite>; a. fr.—V. <cite ref="K01347"><he>כָּתוּב</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: to be written, be reduced to writing; to be written upon.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 1:8">Meg. I, 8</cite> <he>הספרים נִכְתָּבִים בכל לשון</he> the Biblical books may be written in (translated into) any language (v.

<cite ref="Megillah 9a:11">ib. 9ᵃ</cite>); <cite ref="Megillah 9a:11">ib.</cite> <he>לא התירו שׁיִכָּתְבוּ וכ׳</he> they permitted them to be translated only into Greek. Ib. 7ᵃ <he>נאמרה לִיכָּתֵב</he> was indited (by the divine spirit) for the purpose of being written (as a book); <cite ref="Yoma 29a">Yoma 29ᵃ</cite> <he>נתנה ליכתב</he> (some ed. <he>לִכְתּוֹב</he>); a. v. fr.

senses.gloss: to cause to be written or recorded, to dictate, indite.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 22">Gen. R. s. 22</cite> <he>כבר הִכְתַּבְתִּי לך וכ׳</he> I have already ordered to be written in the Law &c.

<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 5:6">Ruth R. to II, 14</cite> <he>אילו היה ראובן יודע שהק״בה מַכְתִּיב עליו וכ׳</he> if R. had known that the Lord would cause to be written about him (<cite ref="Genesis 37:21">Gen. XXXVII, 21</cite>) &c.; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 24">Lev. R. s. 24</cite> <he>ג׳ פרשיות ה׳ לנו וכ׳</he> (<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 15:1">Pesik. R. s. 15</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 307:1">Yalk. Ex. 307</cite> <he>כתכ</he>) there are three sections that Moses indited for us in the Law.

senses.gloss: to consign, enlist in the army, levy.
units: <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15:31">Ex. R. s. 15</cite> (<he>מלך</he>) <he>ב״וד מַכְתִּיב לו וכ׳</he> a human king levies soldiers for himself, strong &c.; Tanḥ. Ḥayé 3 <he>מסביב</he> (corr. acc.).
Cant. R. to II, 8, a. e. מַכְתֶּבֶת, v. טִירוֹנְיָא.—Part. pass. מוּכְתָּב recorded; levied.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 4:5">Kidd. IV, 5</cite>, v. <cite ref="A02413"><he>אִסְטְרַטְיָא</he> II</cite>.—
Tosef. B. Bath. IV, 7; B. Bath. 92ᵇ; Keth. 58ᵃ מ׳ למלכות levied for royal service (comment.: sentenced to death); Kidd. 11ᵃ נִכְתָּב.—

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 89">Gen. R. s. 89</cite> (<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 147:2">Yalk. ib. 147</cite> <cite ref="K01357"><he>כתיב</he></cite>), v. <cite ref="O01505"><he>סַקְרָרִין</he></cite>.
